profile.entities: Airport Authority of India; Mumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC); Mitsubishi; L&T; Delhi Jal Board; Tom Wolf / RIB family fund (German investor partner); GIFT City; National Highway EV Authority; J&K, Gujarat govts
profile.mgmt: Vijay Gupta (Founder, Chairman, MD & CEO); Deepak Bang (CFO); Aadishri Apte (CS & Compliance)
profile.subseg: Building-permit automation (CivitPERMIT/AutoDCR); infra project monitoring (CivitINFRA); construction lifecycle mgmt (CivitBUILD); TDR exchange (Civit TDR); sustainability/IoT (CivitSUSTAIN); digital twin / agentic-AI (CivitTwin); CivitMetaverse
profile.themes: Agentic AI in vertical workflows; digital governance / ease-of-doing-business; infra & urbanization capex; digital twin / BIM-GIS-IoT

deepdive.sec: Construction-Tech / AEC SaaS (vertical software for architecture-engineering-construction & e-governance)

bull_bear.body: - No dividend/buyback discussion on call. Capital primarily reinvested into product R&D (capitalized intangibles) and overseas subsidiary build-out (Germany, US). No net-debt disclosure. Improving working capital is the main internal cash lever (DSO 372→260 days).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Government concentration:** large share of India revenue is govt-linked → slow/uncertain collections (high DSO history), retention/security-deposit drag, multi-corporation negotiation burden; political/budget dependency.
- **Provisioning/receivables:** ~INR 34 cr trade receivables on a small base; aged govt dues require provisioning (some may not reverse on schedule).
- **TDR ramp uncertainty:** revenue depends on transaction volumes migrating on-platform; mandatory only post-10-May; geographic expansion not yet contracted.
- **Overseas execution risk:** Germany/US repeatedly delayed (Germany flagged "huge opportunity" for ~7 yrs); Oman tender stuck at L2 (price) despite T1 (tech), further delayed by war.
- **AI disruption / replication risk:** low-cost AI could replicate permit-check software; moat relies on proprietary data + enterprise penetration.
- **Lumpy, RFP/tender-driven order flow;** lose ~30% of pursued deals, mostly on price.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident and visibly upbeat (maiden call; investor noted "after years of famine, a double shift"). Founder articulate on product vision and govt-impact narrative (credits SoftTech for India's construction-permit ease-of-doing-business rank rising from 183 → ~20). Specific and forthcoming on financials and order economics (TDR take-rate, AAI recognition split, transaction-revenue figures), but appropriately guarded on exact TDR registrations/revenue and on naming new TDR cities. Conservative framing on margins/guidance ("relatively pessimistic," "we may cross").
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- TDR economics: 0.5% take-rate on an INR 8,000 cr/yr BMC market = ~INR 40 cr theoretical at full capture, at 70-80% margin — potentially transformational vs INR 133 cr current revenue, and BMC is only one of several Mumbai-region authorities (MMRDA, MSRDC, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar, Thane all incremental).
- The German entry is not greenfield: it's underwritten by Tom Wolf (founder of RIB, which Schneider bought for ~USD 2.5 bn), a prior SoftTech investor, now investing again via family fund — strong strategic sponsor, not just a customer.
- Transaction-based permit revenue is collected directly from applicants via govt treasury, structurally side-stepping the govt-collection-delay problem that plagues the license model.
- Benchmarks management cites: Procore (construction mgmt), Autodesk and Nemetschek (AEC platforms) — signals ambition/positioning.
- Mitsubishi CivitSUSTAIN win is not yet formally announced (awaiting Mitsubishi Japan HQ publicity approval) — potential under-the-radar catalyst.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

business.body:
- **CivitPERMIT (~50% of revenue):** core building-permit automation (AutoDCR lineage); 1,500+ cities, 18 states; shifting to transaction/pay-per-use (per-permit, sq-ft basis, charged directly to architect/owner via govt treasury → fast cash collection).
- **CivitINFRA (~25%):** infra project monitoring; flagship win = Airport Authority of India (all-airport construction monitoring, BIM-based common data environment, mobile dashboards).
- **CivitBUILD + services (BIM/GIS) (~15-20%):** construction lifecycle management for private enterprises; wins in India + Middle East/Africa.
- **Civit TDR:** new B2B transaction exchange (BMC); high-margin optionality.
- **CivitSUSTAIN:** sustainability/energy/water IoT + digital twin (Mitsubishi water-network win, GIFT City pipeline pending mandate).
- **CivitTwin (newly launched):** agentic-AI plan pre-check / process simulation (12 AI agents, 24×7); launched at Mumbai TechFest by CM Fadnavis; German-market version also launched.
- **CivitMetaverse:** roadmap product connecting site construction to factory/precast construction (metros etc.).
business.title: Segment / product

business.body:
- Govt push on infra/urbanization, digital governance, and ease-of-doing-business → tailwind for SoftTech (permit/infra digitalization).
- Construction industry shift to factory/precast (metros) → CivitMetaverse optionality (site-to-factory connectivity).
- Water infra (Har Ghar Jal, Delhi Jal Board) digitalization → CivitSUSTAIN (with Mitsubishi/L&T).
- ✅/⭐ Listed beneficiaries: (none flagged with high conviction beyond SoftTech itself).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries

latest_quarter.body:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 24% (vs 23% FY25); Q4 21% (vs 15%). Operating leverage improving (PBT/PAT growing far faster than revenue).
- TDR is structurally very high-margin (70-80%; costs limited to data center, app maintenance, integrations, support).
- Cost pressures: gratuity liability up (revised Labour Act, Nov-2025); provisioning policy on aged govt dues.
- Headcount ~550; ~70%+ in R&D/implementation, ~25-30 in business development. Mgmt expects revenue growth to outpace headcount growth (AI leverage), with selective expert hires (metaverse, AI).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost

latest_quarter.body: - **Q4FY26 (this call, maiden):** Rev INR 46.6 cr (+50% YoY, +43% QoQ); FY26 Rev INR 132.9 cr (+40%), EBITDA INR 32.2 cr (24% margin), PAT INR 5.3 cr (+300%+). Order book ~INR 232 cr; pipeline ~INR 436 cr. Marquee wins: AAI CivitINFRA (~INR 16-17 cr), BMC Civit TDR (mandatory 10-May, 0.5% take-rate), Mitsubishi/L&T CivitSUSTAIN, Gujarat/J&K CivitPERMIT, NHEV charging-permit portal. CivitTwin (agentic AI, 12 agents) launched. DSO 372→260 days. Guidance: ~INR 300 cr revenue by FY29 at 28-30% EBITDA; FY27 +25-27%. One-offs: provisions up to ~INR 2.5 cr (aged govt dues + Nov-25 gratuity). Germany subsidiary live (Tom Wolf/RIB sponsor); Oman tender stuck at L2 (war-delayed).
latest_quarter.title: QoQ log

outlook.body:
- **Revenue: ~INR 300 cr in 3 years (by FY29)** — from ~INR 133 cr FY26 base (implies ~31% CAGR). Mgmt called this "achievable" and even "relatively pessimistic / we may cross."
- **FY27 growth: 25-27%** on all ongoing businesses (~20% on core ongoing + TDR uplift + some Germany/US/Middle-East additions).
- **EBITDA margin: 25-30% minimum near-term; 28-30% sustainable** at the INR 300 cr scale (conservative); upside if TDR (70-80% margin) and overseas mix rise.
- **FY27 revenue mix (by product):** CivitPERMIT ~50% (could rise; flagship, transaction-based projects going live); CivitINFRA ~25% (flat-to-slightly-lower); CivitBUILD + BIM/GIS services ~15-20%.
- **Geography target (3 yr):** ~50% India, rising overseas share over time.
- **TDR:** not all of the theoretical ~INR 40 cr (0.5% × INR 8,000 cr) lands in FY27 (mandatory only from 10-May; pre-10-May transactions still off-platform) — partial contribution in FY27, ramping over subsequent quarters.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)

outlook.body:
- **Total order book ~INR 232 cr** (of the ~INR 200 cr core, ~60% to be booked as FY27 revenue, of which ~40% recurring).
- **Opportunity pipeline ~INR 436 cr**, with mgmt-claimed **>60% conversion probability** (they engage pre-RFP and bid selectively; ~70% win rate, lose ~30% mainly on price/underbidding).
- **Airport Authority of India (CivitINFRA):** ~INR 16-17 cr order (incl. GST), one-time license; ~40% recognized in FY26, remaining ~60% over next ~3 years; first phase successful, scope for large future enhancements (digital twinning, remote project control).
- **BMC Civit TDR exchange:** live, mandatory from 10-May-2026; ~100+ registrations, a few trades done; revenue = 0.5% of transaction value on a market that did ~INR 8,000 cr/yr in BMC alone (theoretical ~INR 40 cr at full capture); replicable to MMRDA, MSRDC, Navi Mumbai, Vasai-Virar, Thane, and other cities/states.
- New mandates: CivitPERMIT for Gujarat; J&K GIS master-plan/single-window; National Highway EV charging-station permit portal; CivitSUSTAIN first order (Mitsubishi/L&T, Delhi Jal Board water network).
outlook.title: Order book / pipeline

outlook.body:
- **TDR exchange replication** across Indian cities/states — mgmt: "entire country now looking at TDR"; SoftTech advantaged via its existing permit add-on that automates TDR generation/allocation/utilization (e.g., most Mumbai TDRs over past 4-5 yrs generated on its platform).
- **Germany:** subsidiary set up (acquired a shell co held by Sandy Moser; recruited German sales leader); prototyping with select customers next ~3 months; commercial traction expected ~Q3/Q4 FY27; launching both digital-twin and permitting portal; backed by RIB-founder Tom Wolf's family fund (Wolf invested via family fund after RIB sold to Schneider for ~USD 2.5 bn).
- **US:** product aligned to IBC/IRC codes; small private-sector revenue already in FY25-26; partner traction; bigger orders targeted FY26-27.
- **Transaction/recurring shift:** transaction-based revenue grew from ~INR 20-23 cr (FY25) to ~INR 31-32 cr (FY26), ~40-45% growth — structurally improves cash flow and lowers receivables.
- **Agentic AI** leveraging 15 yrs of proprietary permits dataset ("gold mine") as a moat.
outlook.title: Growth / optionality

deepdive.thesis: SoftTech is a ~3-decade-old, founder-led vertical software product company for the architecture-engineering-construction-and-operations (AECO) domain, anchored by a dominant building-permit automation franchise (claims ~80% market share in permitting; AutoDCR/CivitPERMIT live in 1,500+ cities, 18 states). FY26 was an inflection: maiden conference call, revenue +40% to INR 132.9 cr, PAT 4x to INR 5.3 cr, and several marquee wins (Airport Authority of India CivitINFRA, BMC Civit TDR exchange, Mitsubishi/L&T CivitSUSTAIN water project). The thesis is (a) a deepening shift from one-time-license to recurring + transaction-based revenue (improving cash flow / DSO), (b) high-margin optionality from the BMC TDR exchange (0.5% of transaction value, INR 8,000 cr/yr TDR volume in BMC alone, 70-80% margin), and (c) export optionality (Germany via RIB-founder Tom Wolf, US, Middle East). Management targets ~INR 300 cr revenue in 3 years (FY29) at 28-30% EBITDA margin.
